c.tagline: Laid-back Sichuan capital of pandas, teahouses, and mouth-numbing hotpot.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around ¥8-9; most residents book via Didi, and drivers overwhelmingly expect Alipay or WeChat Pay rather than cash.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police, 120 for ambulance, and 119 for fire; English-language support is limited, so having a translation app or local help ready is useful.

hood_landmark.Jinjiang / Chunxi Road: Sino-Ocean Taikoo Li Chunxi Road, Chengdu
hood_landmark.Qingyang / Kuanzhai Alley: Kuanzhai Alley (Wide and Narrow Alleys), Chengdu

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in crowded Chunxi Road and metro stations, and decline overly friendly invitations to teahouses or bars that can end in inflated bills.

hood_desc: Central downtown core around the Chunxi Road pedestrian street and the open-air Sino-Ocean Taikoo Li mall; best for first-timers who want shopping, food, and metro links all within walking distance.
The historic heart with the Qing-era Kuanzhai Alley (Wide and Narrow Alleys), the Qingyang Palace Taoist temple, and People's Park teahouses; best for old-Chengdu atmosphere and sightseeing.
Home to the Wuhou Shrine (Three Kingdoms memorial), the reconstructed Jinli Ancient Street, and a lively Tibetan quarter; best for culture, street snacks, and evening strolls.
Chengdu's modern high-tech and financial district of skyscrapers, the New Century Global Center, and Jiaozi Park; suits business travelers and those wanting new malls and calmer, newer surroundings.
A practical transit-hub district around Chengdu North Railway Station with wholesale markets and inexpensive hotels; convenient for onward high-speed rail and budget stays.
lodging: Ji Hotel Chengdu Gaoxin Financial Center
Home Inn Chengdu North Railway Station
7 Days Inn Chengdu North Railway Station

water.note: Tap water meets basic standards but isn't recommended to drink untreated; stick to bottled water.

transit.hours: Metro trains run roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; buses run from early morning to around 10-11 PM, with Didi and taxis covering later hours.
transit.note: Chengdu Metro is one of China's largest systems, with 17+ lines topping 720 km, backed by an extensive bus network and a tram line in the outer districts.
transit.pay: Fares start at ¥2 by distance; pay with the Tianfutong transit card, a QR code via the Tianfutong or Alipay app, or single-ride tickets from station machines. Cash is rarely used.

bus: Intercity coaches from Chadianzi, Beimen, and Xinnanmen bus stations

car.idp: Not recognized (a temporary or full Chinese driving license is required)

train: Chengdu East, Chengdu South & Chengdu North railway stations (high-speed rail to Chongqing, Xi'an, Kunming and beyond)

transit.m: Metro Line 10 from Shuangliu Airport to the center (~30 min, transfer to Line 3/1)
Airport shuttle buses to key downtown points; note the newer Chengdu Tianfu Int'l (TFU), ~50 km SE, handles most long-haul flights and links by Metro Line 18 / airport rail

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in Chengdu; restaurant bills are paid as-is and rounding up is neither required nor common.

food.name: Mapo Tofu
food.desc: Silky tofu cubes simmered in fiery chili-bean sauce with minced beef and ground Sichuan pepper, numbing and blisteringly red. Invented here in 1862.

places.name: Chen Mapo Tofu (Qinghua Road flagship)
places.note: The original 1862 house, still the benchmark; expect a queue at peak hours.

places.name: Chen Mapo Tofu (Luomashi branch)
places.note: Central, less crowded branch of the same institution; easy to reach by metro.

places.name: Kuanzhai Alley Sichuan restaurants
places.note: Restored Qing courtyard restaurants serving mapo tofu alongside the full Sichuan canon.

food.name: Dan Dan Noodles
food.desc: A small bowl of thin noodles over chili oil, sesame and preserved vegetable, topped with crisp minced pork. Tossed at the table, eaten in a few bites.

places.name: Long Chaoshou
places.note: Famous snack hall doing dan dan noodles alongside nearly every other Chengdu classic.

places.name: Kuanzhai Alley snack stalls
places.note: Row of small snack windows where you order noodles, san da pao and dumplings one at a time.

places.name: Wenshu Monastery lane eateries
places.note: Old-town noodle shops near the temple, popular with locals for a cheap morning bowl.

food.name: Sichuan Hotpot
food.desc: A cauldron of beef-tallow broth loaded with chilies and Sichuan pepper; dip tripe, beef and vegetables, then cool them in sesame oil and garlic.

places.name: Huangcheng Laoma Hotpot (Qintai Road)
places.note: Long-running upscale hotpot house with drinkable broth and a split pot for beginners.

places.name: Houtang Hot Pot
places.note: Consistently top-ranked for bold, properly numbing broth; central and used to visitors.

places.name: Shu Jiu Xiang Hotpot
places.note: Reliable local chain with English-friendly menus and quality beef tallow broth.

food.name: Red-Oil Chaoshou
food.desc: Chengdu wontons with paper-thin skins floating in sweetened soy and chili oil rather than soup. A softer heat than most Sichuan dishes.

places.name: Long Chaoshou
places.note: The name means Dragon Wonton; its skins are legendarily thin. The definitive spot.

places.name: Kuanzhai Alley snack houses
places.note: Good for sampling chaoshou next to Zhong dumplings and Lai tangyuan in one sitting.

food.name: Chuan Chuan Xiang
food.desc: Hotpot on skewers: grab sticks of meat and vegetables from a fridge, cook them in shared chili broth, and pay by the stick at the end.

places.name: Yulin district skewer joints
places.note: The city's late-night neighborhood for chuan chuan, plastic stools and cheap beer included.

places.name: Jinli Street food lane
places.note: Tourist-friendly stretch of skewers and snacks beside Wuhou Shrine; good for a first try.

food.name: Chengdu Snack Platter
food.desc: The classic sampler: Zhong sweet-soy dumplings, Lai tangyuan sesame rice balls, sweet water noodles and san da pao rice cakes, all in tiny portions.

places.name: Long Chaoshou
places.note: Order the set platter of a dozen classic snacks to taste the whole repertoire at once.

places.name: Kuanzhai Alley
places.note: Walk-and-eat street with san da pao pounded to order and sweet water noodles by the bowl.

food.name: Gaiwan Jasmine Tea
food.desc: Green or jasmine tea served in a lidded gaiwan and topped up endlessly from a long-spouted copper kettle. The heart of Chengdu teahouse culture.

places.name: Heming Teahouse
places.note: Open since 1923; bamboo chairs, mahjong, roving ear-cleaners and cheap free-refill gaiwans.

places.name: Kuanzhai Alley teahouses
places.note: Courtyard teahouses with Sichuan opera face-changing shows in the evenings.

places.name: Wenshu Monastery teahouse
places.note: Tranquil temple-garden tea tables, a calmer alternative to People's Park.

food.name: Suan Mei Tang
food.desc: Iced sour plum drink made from smoked plums, hawthorn and osmanthus. The traditional antidote to a mouthful of Sichuan chili and peppercorn.

places.name: Huangcheng Laoma Hotpot
places.note: Served by the jug alongside the pot; the standard local pairing with hotpot.

places.name: Hotpot houses citywide
places.note: Nearly every hotpot restaurant serves it free or cheap in refillable pitchers.

landmarks: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
A world-renowned sanctuary where visitors can watch giant pandas roam bamboo groves, making it Chengdu's most beloved and photographed attraction.
Jinli Ancient Street
A beautifully restored Qing-dynasty-style pedestrian street strung with red lanterns, teahouses, and traditional Sichuan architecture.
Kuanzhai Alley (Wide and Narrow Alley)
A trio of historic hutong-style lanes blending Qing-era courtyard architecture with modern boutiques, capturing old and new Chengdu side by side.
Wuhou Shrine (Wuhou Temple)
A revered temple honoring the Three Kingdoms statesman Zhuge Liang, prized for its ancient cypress trees, red walls, and classical Chinese gardens.
Jinsha Site Museum
An archaeological site preserving a 3,000-year-old ancient Shu civilization settlement, home to the famed golden sun-and-immortal-bird artifact.
Leshan Giant Buddha
The world's largest carved stone Buddha, a 71-meter statue overlooking the confluence of three rivers near Chengdu, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Mount Qingcheng
One of Taoism's birthplaces, this lush, misty mountain near Chengdu is famed for ancient temples and dense forest trails, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Du Fu Thatched Cottage
The tranquil former residence of Tang-dynasty poet Du Fu, now a serene garden memorial celebrating one of China's greatest literary figures.
Tianfu Square
The bustling civic heart of modern Chengdu, anchored by a monumental Mao Zedong statue and surrounded by museums and skyscrapers.
Chunxi Road
Chengdu's flashy, neon-lit main shopping district, a dazzling hub of fashion, food, and nightlife emblematic of the city's modern energy.

train.note: Chengdu has no international passenger trains - the well-publicised Chengdu-Europe services are freight only. Chengdu East is the main hub, on the Chengdu-Chongqing intercity line (about 1.5 hours), the Xi'an-Chengdu high-speed line (about 3 hours) and the Chengdu-Guiyang high-speed line towards Guiyang and Kunming, with Chengdu South, West and North handling other services. Sleeper trains run west and north to Xining and on to Lhasa, and these need booking as far ahead as the window allows. Book on 12306 with your passport; foreign passport holders can also use Trip.com.

bus.note: No scheduled international coaches leave Chengdu. Xinnanmen (Traffic Hotel) bus station beside the Jinjiang River is the traveller's terminal, with departures for Leshan, Emeishan, Jiuzhaigou and Kangding; Chadianzi station in the north-west covers western Sichuan and the Tibetan prefectures, and Beimen station serves northern routes. Tickets are sold at the counters and on Chinese apps, and buses remain the only public transport to much of western Sichuan where the railway does not reach.

ferry.note: Chengdu is well inland on the Sichuan basin and has no passenger ferry services. For Yangtze River cruises you need to start at Chongqing, about 1.5 hours away by high-speed train.

half.name: Sanxingdui Museum
half.blurb: A museum displaying startling bronze masks and artifacts from the mysterious Bronze Age Shu civilization, unearthed in the 1980s.

half.name: Dujiangyan Irrigation System
half.blurb: A functioning 3rd-century-BC engineering marvel that still channels the Min River to irrigate the Chengdu plain without a dam.

half.name: Huanglongxi Ancient Town
half.blurb: A well-preserved Qing-dynasty river town of stone streets, old banyan trees and traditional teahouses south of the city.

full.name: Xiling Snow Mountain
full.blurb: A ski resort and forested peak in the mountains west of Chengdu, with cable cars, alpine scenery and winter snow sports.

full.name: Siguniang Mountain (Four Sisters Mountain)
full.blurb: A dramatic four-peaked massif and nature reserve in the Qionglai range, a gateway to Tibetan-influenced valleys and glacier views.
